title: "Jackson's Nook" and bop-flavored blues with Pony Poindexter
summary: He recorded "Jackson's Nook" in San Francisco at a club owned by a Jackson, and says he had to keep up with the times.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, now, you did a recording that was very much like a bop blues recording, the one with Penny Pinty Poindexter.
Yeah.
Do you remember that?
I forget now.

It was like a riff -- well, in some ways it was like a swing riff tune, like one of the Lionel Hampton type tunes, but the drummer and the bass player were giving that bop feeling, because of the way the drummer was --
What was the name of it?
-- hitting the cymbal. I'm trying to remember that. Let me look that up.
With Pony? Pointy?
Yeah. In the '50s. "Jackson's Nook".
"Jacksons Nook."
Remember that? And then, "I've Come A Long Ways Baby."
"I've Come A Long Ways Baby."
Which was more of a traditional blues. But "Jackson's Nook", you know, definitely had that bop feeling.
Uh-huh. That was up in Frisco.
Uh-huh.
That was taken up in Frisco, "Jackson's Nook."
Oh, really?
Yeah. He had that and I used to play in there all the time, you know? And he had it, it was the Nook, and I named it Jackson's Nook because his name was Jackson.
Uh-huh.
They had owned the place and --
The club. That would have been around somewhere in '52, something like that?
Probably so, yeah.
Yeah. But then like in other words you were trying to keep up with the trend as much as you could but still maintain your own feeling.
Yeah. I had to keep up with it, you know?
Uh-huh. How did you feel --
That was the thought.
Yeah.
I had to keep up with it. It was the times.
